sections.markdown:
# Distractions, collisions, emergencies and adverse weather

FACT_ID: sec14-F01 | anchor: A01
No preparation can eliminate every driving hazard, but recognizing hazards helps a driver respond. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec14-F02 | anchor: A01
Before departure, check the travel path, adjust the seat and mirrors, buckle occupants and remove distractions. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec14-F03 | anchor: A01
Visual distraction diverts the eyes, manual distraction occupies the hands and cognitive distraction diverts attention. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec14-F04 | anchor: A01
Texting combines visual, manual and cognitive distraction. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec14-F05 | anchor: A01
Eating, grooming, passenger conversation, navigation use and entertainment controls can distract a driver. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0115]

FACT_ID: sec14-F06 | anchor: A02
A hands-free device can still cause cognitive distraction even while both hands remain available. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F07 | anchor: A02
Silence or turn off the phone before driving to reduce the temptation to respond. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F08 | anchor: A02
Pull into a safe location before making a necessary call or ask a passenger to make it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F09 | anchor: A02
Study unfamiliar routes before setting out rather than reading directions while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F10 | anchor: A02
Secure pets before departure and stop safely before attending to a child’s needs. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F11 | anchor: A02
Do not reach for an item that falls inside the vehicle while driving. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0116]

FACT_ID: sec14-F12 | anchor: A03
The guide groups collision contributors into equipment problems, roadway design, road maintenance and driver behavior. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F13 | anchor: A03
Unsafe tires, braking or steering faults can contribute to a collision. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F14 | anchor: A03
Road debris, potholes and construction can create collision hazards. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F15 | anchor: A03
Tailgating, unsafe lane changes, speeding and failing to yield are hazardous driver behaviors. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0117]

FACT_ID: sec14-F16 | anchor: A04
Store loose objects in the trunk when possible so they are less likely to strike occupants in a collision. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F17 | anchor: A04
The guide recommends keeping writing materials, insurance details and emergency supplies in a collision kit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F18 | anchor: A04
Know which braking system the vehicle has; the owner’s manual can identify anti-lock equipment. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F19 | anchor: A04
Anti-lock braking helps preserve steering control by managing wheel lockup. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F20 | anchor: A04
A persistent ABS warning lamp indicates that the system needs attention. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F21 | anchor: A04
If an approaching vehicle enters the driver’s lane, avoid escaping into the opposing lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0118]

FACT_ID: sec14-F22 | anchor: A05
Wear the lap-and-shoulder belt before every trip as protection if a collision cannot be avoided. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec14-F23 | anchor: A05
A sideways-sliding vehicle can roll when a curb, soft ground or another obstruction trips it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec14-F24 | anchor: A05
A higher center of gravity makes a vehicle more prone to tipping. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0119]

FACT_ID: sec14-F25 | anchor: A06
Excess speed and abrupt steering can contribute to a rollover. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F26 | anchor: A06
If the vehicle leaves the pavement, slow gradually rather than jerking the steering wheel back toward the road. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F27 | anchor: A06
Belts help prevent occupants from being ejected during a rollover. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F28 | anchor: A06
Some side airbags use rollover sensors to help protect occupants during a rollover. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F29 | anchor: A06
Abrupt turning or stopping on a slippery surface can cause a skid. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F30 | anchor: A06
In the guide’s rear-skid example, turn toward the direction in which the rear is sliding without oversteering. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0120]

FACT_ID: sec14-F31 | anchor: A07
Braking and steering responses can vary with the vehicle’s drive and control systems. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F32 | anchor: A07
Avoid abrupt steering during traction loss and look toward the desired travel path. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F33 | anchor: A07
Electronic stability control compares the intended direction with actual vehicle travel and can apply individual brakes to help maintain stability. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F34 | anchor: A07
When hydroplaning, avoid a sudden turn or sudden braking and ease off the accelerator. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0121]

FACT_ID: sec14-F35 | anchor: A07
If trapped on tracks with a train approaching, get all occupants out and away from the rail path. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-la-e:louisiana-office-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0121]
